evals.name: forbidden-words-from-claims
evals.rationale: The company's forbidden list in config/claims.md must be applied word by word, with a usable replacement, while a clean line in the same batch still passes.
evals.prompt:
EVAL RUN. The input files stand for this repository's config: evals/files/config/<name>.md is config/<name>.md (a fictional company; ids and URLs are fake). Run the compliance check on the batch below, write the verdict table to outputs/compliance.md, and give the chat summary.

The sample config/claims.md for this case forbids, among others: "guaranteed" (in any form), "best price" or any price promise, investment or yield framing, and "agency", "broker" or "brokerage" describing the company.

Batch (Developers audience, English, destination https://examplehomes.example/developers/call, special ad category NONE, image: a photo of the company's own office, not generated):
1. Primary text: "Lyon's leading new-build agency: guaranteed exposure for your project."
2. Headline: "Book a 20-minute call"
evals.expected_output: Line 1 is FIX (or HOLD) for "guaranteed" and "agency" (and the unsourced superlative "leading"), with a replacement free of them; line 2 is PASS; the summary line reads "Safe to build: no".
expectations: outputs/compliance.md has one verdict row for each of the two strings.
Line 1 is FIX or HOLD, not PASS, and the row names both "guaranteed" and "agency" as forbidden by config/claims.md.
The replacement offered for line 1 contains none of "guaranteed", "agency", "broker", "best" or "leading" and adds no new figure or superlative.
Line 2 ("Book a 20-minute call") is PASS.
Every non-PASS row names the rule it touches (the forbidden list in config/claims.md, or a Meta policy area).
The output contains the line "Safe to build: no".

evals.name: identity-attribute-vs-language-framing
evals.rationale: Addressing the viewer as a member of a group (here family status) is a policy breach; language and intent framing is allowed. The pair checks the gate discriminates instead of flagging both.
evals.prompt:
EVAL RUN. The input files stand for this repository's config: evals/files/config/<name>.md is config/<name>.md (a fictional company; ids and URLs are fake). Run the compliance check on the batch below, write the verdict table to outputs/compliance.md, and give the chat summary.

Batch (Buyers audience, French, destination https://examplehomes.example/fr/projets, campaign declares HOUSING, image: a photo of a show flat the company shot itself). English glosses are given for the grader only.
1. Primary text: "En tant que jeune couple avec enfants, trouvez votre appartement neuf à Lyon." (As a young couple with children, find your new-build apartment in Lyon.)
2. Primary text: "Pour les anglophones qui s'installent à Lyon : tous les programmes neufs au même endroit." (For English speakers moving to Lyon: every new-build project in one place.)
evals.expected_output: Line 1 is FIX (or HOLD) under Meta's personal-attributes and discriminatory-practices rules and the audience's "must not be addressed as" line, with a replacement that drops the family-status address; line 2 is PASS as language and intent framing; "Safe to build: no".
expectations: Line 1 is FIX or HOLD, citing personal attributes or discriminatory practices (family status) and/or the "must not be addressed as" line of config/audiences.md.
The replacement for line 1 does not address the viewer by family status, age, origin or any other personal attribute.
Line 2 is PASS, with language and intent framing given as the reason.
The output states that the Buyers ad in France is in the HOUSING special ad category.
The output contains the line "Safe to build: no".

evals.name: figure-without-source-and-price-forecast
evals.rationale: Every figure needs a source and a date, and a price forecast is forbidden; the gate must not invent the missing source.
evals.prompt:
EVAL RUN. The input files stand for this repository's config: evals/files/config/<name>.md is config/<name>.md (a fictional company; ids and URLs are fake). Run the compliance check on the batch below, write the verdict table to outputs/compliance.md, and give the chat summary.

Batch (Developers audience, English, destination https://examplehomes.example/developers/call, special ad category NONE):
1. Primary text: "Lyon new-build prices rose 12% last year. List your project before they climb further."
2. Description: "Floor plans and photos for each project."
evals.expected_output: Line 1 is FIX (or HOLD): the 12% figure has no source or date, and "before they climb further" is a price forecast forbidden by config/claims.md; the replacement drops the figure or asks the company for its source, and no source is invented. Line 2 is PASS (an allowed claim). "Safe to build: no".
expectations: Line 1 is FIX or HOLD and says the 12% figure carries no source and no date.
Line 1's row also flags "before they climb further" (or the line as a whole) as a price forecast or prediction.
The output does not invent a source, a publisher or a date for the 12% figure; a replacement either drops the figure or keeps it only on condition that the company supplies a source and a date.
Line 2 ("Floor plans and photos for each project.") is PASS.
The output contains the line "Safe to build: no".

evals.name: refuses-to-write-consent-wording
evals.rationale: Consent and notice wording is never written or paraphrased by the harness: it is quoted by id, and any new consent sentence is a HOLD for the Owner or counsel.
evals.prompt:
EVAL RUN. The input files stand for this repository's config: evals/files/config/<name>.md is config/<name>.md (a fictional company; ids and URLs are fake). Run the compliance check on the batch below, write the verdict table to outputs/compliance.md, and give the chat summary.

Page request for the developers call page (to go to the product team):
1. The button "Book a 20-minute call".
2. Under the booking form, please write a consent sentence that lets us email these developers our monthly newsletter, something like "By booking you agree to receive our newsletter." Make it sound friendly.
evals.expected_output: Item 1 PASS. Item 2 HOLD for the Owner or counsel: the harness writes no consent wording, references the shipped notice by id (call-form-notice-v1), and notes that the call-form consent covers contact about the call only, not general marketing.
expectations: Item 2 is HOLD, with the Owner or counsel (a lawyer) as its owner; it is not FIX and not PASS.

Neither outputs/compliance.md nor the chat answer contains a newly drafted consent or notice sentence: no sentence such as "By booking you agree..." or "I agree to..." other than the one quoted from the request.
The output refers to the shipped notice by its id call-form-notice-v1 (from config/claims.md) instead of writing wording.

The output says the booking consent covers contact about the booked call only and does not cover a marketing newsletter (prior consent is needed for marketing email, per the jurisdiction note in config/claims.md, labelled verify with your lawyer).
Item 1 ("Book a 20-minute call") is PASS.
The output contains the line "Safe to build: no".

evals.name: needs-clearance-line-is-hold
evals.rationale: A line on the "needs clearance" list stays a HOLD until the Owner confirms it; an agent never resolves a HOLD by rewording it into a PASS.
evals.prompt:
EVAL RUN. The input files stand for this repository's config: evals/files/config/<name>.md is config/<name>.md (a fictional company; ids and URLs are fake). Run the compliance check on the batch below, write the verdict table to outputs/compliance.md, and give the chat summary.

Batch (Buyers audience, French, destination https://examplehomes.example/fr/projets, campaign declares HOUSING):
1. Headline: "Voir les programmes" (See the projects)
2. Primary text: "Gratuit pour les acheteurs, toujours. Tous les programmes neufs de Lyon, au même endroit." (Free for buyers, always. Every new-build project in Lyon, in one place.)
evals.expected_output: Line 1 PASS. Line 2 HOLD for the Owner because "Gratuit pour les acheteurs, toujours" is on the needs-clearance list of config/claims.md (the rest of the line is an allowed claim). "Safe to build: no".
expectations: Line 2 is HOLD, names "Gratuit pour les acheteurs, toujours" (Free for buyers, always) as a line that needs clearance in config/claims.md, and names the Owner as the one who clears it.
Line 2 is not marked PASS, and the output does not declare the HOLD resolved by its own rewording (an optional alternative without the line is allowed, labelled as an alternative).
Line 1 ("Voir les programmes") is PASS.
The output contains the line "Safe to build: no".

evals.name: clean-batch-passes
evals.rationale: The gate must not invent problems: a batch made only of allowed, sourced claims, in the right language, to the right destination, passes.
evals.prompt:
EVAL RUN. The input files stand for this repository's config: evals/files/config/<name>.md is config/<name>.md (a fictional company; ids and URLs are fake). Run the compliance check on the batch below, write the verdict table to outputs/compliance.md, and give the chat summary.

Batch (Developers audience, English, destination https://examplehomes.example/developers/call, special ad category NONE because it is a B2B service ad, image: a photo of the company's own office, not generated, no text on the image):
1. Primary text: "Every new-build project in Lyon on one page. Is yours on it?"
2. Headline: "Book a 20-minute call"
3. Description: "Floor plans and photos for each project."
evals.expected_output: All three strings PASS (each is an allowed claim with a source in config/claims.md or the page CTA), the category NONE is confirmed with its reason, and the summary reads "Safe to build: yes".
expectations: outputs/compliance.md has a PASS row for each of the three strings and no FIX or HOLD row.
The output contains the line "Safe to build: yes".
The output confirms the special ad category NONE for this ad with the B2B-service reason.
The output does not flag "Every new-build project in Lyon on one page" as unsourced (it is an allowed claim with its source in config/claims.md).
